findings.body:
The findings schema example always injects a `complexity` field, and when `require_complexity=False` (the **default** for most consumers) it includes a `// optional` JavaScript comment inside a ` ```json ` fence.

Failure mode: agent-runner models that template from the example write non-JSON (`json.loads` fails). With `allow_malformed_summary_fallback=True` that degrades to **summary-only** — every inline finding is dropped (`docs/PROVIDERS.md` § malformed CLI JSON fallback). This is a regression on the default complexity-off path; previously the schema had no such comment.

Fix: only emit the `complexity` key in the fenced example when `require_complexity` is true, and never put `//` comments inside the JSON example. Put optional notes in the Rules section instead.

With `complexity-labels-enabled: true` on **every** matrix leg, each provider calls `gh_remove_labels_by_prefix` + `gh_apply_label` for the same `complexity:` prefix. Legs finish at different times and can disagree on `low|medium|high`, so the final label is nondeterministic (last writer wins) and intermediate remove/apply races can briefly clear the label.

Before this PR only chat-completions actually applied complexity labels; agent-runners no-oped. Enabling the bridge on a multi-provider matrix introduces thrash that dashboards / routing rules will see as flaky.

Fix: enable complexity labeling on a single designated leg (e.g. `anthropic` only), or document and accept last-writer semantics for multi-provider consumers in `docs/PR_METADATA_CHECKS.md` / `docs/PROVIDERS.md`.

`infer_pr_complexity_fallback` treats any path containing the substrings `auth`, `token`, `secret`, etc. as `high`. That over-fires on ordinary paths: `tests/test_author.py` matches `auth`, `docs/token-guide.md` matches `token`, `oauth_client.py` matches `auth` via `oauth`.

This matters because the fallback always runs when the model omits `complexity` (still common even with a "required" prompt rule), and `action.yml` / README / `PR_METADATA_CHECKS.md` advertise cognitive-load labeling that is **not** line-count based — yet the fallback also uses `additions+deletions` thresholds (`>100` / `>500`). Downstream routing on `complexity:high` will then mis-route.

Fix: match path segments (split on `/` / `_` / `-`) or an allowlist of known security paths; keep line-count only as a weak tie-break and say so in the docs; prefer leaving the label unset over a misleading heuristic if the model omitted the field.

summary:
## Verdict

Solid provider-bridge for complexity labels — the `findings.json` field, unified post-review apply path, and test coverage are the right shape. Three warnings should be fixed before merge: an invalid JSON example in the agent-runner output contract (default path), multi-provider label thrash on dogfood, and a brittle heuristic fallback.

## Findings

| # | Severity | File | Summary |
|---|----------|------|---------|
| 1 | ⚠️ warning | `scripts/reviewer.py:5645` | Schema example embeds `// optional` (invalid JSON) on the default agent-runner path |
| 2 | ⚠️ warning | `.github/workflows/self-review.yml:331` | Every matrix leg applies `complexity:*` — last writer wins |
| 3 | ⚠️ warning | `scripts/reviewer.py:5443` | Heuristic markers use bare substrings (`auth`⊂`author`); also line-count based while docs claim otherwise |

## Notes

- Runtime stays stdlib-only; no new subprocess/shell, path, or secret surfaces.
- Public contract preserved (optional behavior only); docs matrix + setup reference + CHANGELOG are in sync for the agent-runner bridge.
- `parse_complexity_level` / `resolve_pr_complexity` / noop-warning regression tests look correct; targeted unittest subset passed.
- Self-review gate rename `AIReview` → `ready` matches existing docs/TRIGGER_MODES.md and AGENTS.md.

**Recommendation:** request-changes
